messages.content: 你能計算從地球到一個新發現的距離為4.22光年的外行星，再到另一個距離第一顆外行星6.1光年的外行星，最後再回到距離第二顆外行星5.88光年的地球所需的時間嗎？假設真空中光的速度為299792458公尺/秒。

function.name: light_travel_time
function.description: Calculate the time taken for light to travel from a celestial body to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

distance_in_light_years.description: The distance between the two celestial bodies in light years. This is a float type value.

speed_of_light.description: The speed of light in vacuum, in m/s. Default value is 299792458 m/s.

Wait "another planet 6.1 light-years away from the first exoplanet" So second leg distance=6.1 ly. Then back to Earth which is 5.88 ly away from second exoplanet. Sum distances: 4.22 + 6.1 + 5.88 = 16.2 ly.

Compute time: convert ly to meters: 1 ly ≈ c * year seconds. Light travels one light-year per year obviously; but we can use formula: time = distance / speed. Since distance given as light-years and speed same units? We could just sum times: each leg takes its distance in years because speed equals c. But they gave speed explicitly maybe want conversion to seconds or days. Let's calculate total time in years: 16.2 years. Convert to days: multiply by 365.25 ~ 5920 days. In hours: 142k hrs etc. Provide answer with explanation.

But might also ask to use function light_travel_time. That expects distance in light years and returns something unspecified. We'll call it thrice? Actually we have three legs: 4.22, 6.1, 5.88.
